title: Usage conciliation adjudicator for late/multi-route token events
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: We continue to see reconciliation drift between real-time ingestion events (edge/route collectors) and the canonical billing ledger. Causes include out-of-order deliveries from edge collectors, multi-route splits where a single user request spawns multiple model calls, and delayed enrichment jobs that attach cost attributes. Problem: This drift produces incorrect short-term console metrics and occasional invoice adjustments for a subset of customers with interleaved multi-route workloads. Goal: Implement a resilient, idempotent "conciliation adjudicator" worker that merges near-real-time usage events with the ledger using a deterministic fingerprinting strategy, time-windowed convergence, and a confidence score to mark events for auto-apply vs manual review.
acceptance_criteria: New adjudicator processes stream of raw usage events and produces reconciled deltas against ledger with idempotency guarantees (no duplicate ledger writes).
End-to-end shadow run shows <0.1% divergence vs current ledger for a 24h sample and explains 90% of previously unexplained late-arrival adjustments.
Canary deployment handles 10k events/s in production region with median processing latency < 90s and P95 < 3m under normal load.
Operator dashboard with reconciliation rate, late-arrival histogram, confidence-score distribution, and top root causes implemented and alerts created.
Backfill plan validated in staging and can be executed without double-credits; runbook documented.
tasks: Design schema for adjudication record (fingerprint, confidence, source_tags, route_map, dedupe_token)
Implement deterministic fingerprinting util in ingestion library and add to route collectors
Build adjudicator worker: windowing, merge rules, confidence scoring, idempotent ledger writes
Add reconciliation consumer to ledger service with safe-upsert API and audit trail
Integration tests: out-of-order, duplicate, multi-route split cases
Shadow-run for 72h against production traffic (read-only) and compare diffs
Canary rollout (5% tenants) and metrics validation
Backfill job to reconcile last 30 days with safety caps
Operator docs, runbooks, and console dashboard widgets
design_decisions: Windowing: use 2-minute rolling windows for primary reconciliation with a separate late-arrival window up to 48 hours for low-confidence events
Fingerprint: sha256(customer_id || route_id || request_prefix_hash || timestamp_bucket) to balance collision risk and late-arrival matching
Idempotency: ledger exposes safe_upsert(fingerprint, delta, source_meta) with strict monotonic sequence enforcement
Confidence scoring: deterministic rule-based score with features (arrival_delta, route_siblings, token_count_match, model_variant_match). Events below threshold go to manual review queue
Backfill: run in read-only shadow mode first; apply only after manual verification of sampling and verifying no duplicates.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy fingerprinting lib to collectors (non-breaking) and monitor fingerprint presence metric
2) Deploy adjudicator in shadow mode (no writes) for 72h, collect diffs and surface top unexplained deltas
3) Iterate heuristics and tune confidence thresholds based on shadow-run findings
4) Enable safe_upsert on ledger with throttles and circuit breaker
5) Start canary apply for 5% of tenants with heavy monitoring
6) Gradually increase apply from 5% -> 25% -> 100% across 48-72h windows
7) Schedule backfill for past 30 days with per-tenant rate limits and manual verification checkpoints
rollback_plan: If reconciliation write rate or error rate exceeds thresholds: flip adjudicator to shadow mode immediately and re-run observed diffs for manual reconciliation
If ledger safe_upsert causes constraint errors: disable safe_upsert and route adjudicator outputs to S3 for offline processing
If double-credits observed: pause applies, run compensation run that reverses suspect fingerprints using ledger audit trail
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and deterministic scoring
Integration tests simulating multi-route split and out-of-order deliveries
Staging-scale shadow run using production replay for 24h sample
Chaos tests: delayed events, duplicate bursts, partial collector failures
End-to-end billing simulation comparing expected invoice lines before and after reconciliation
observability_requirements: Distributed traces: span for fingerprint->merge->ledger_upsert with request_id propagation
Dashboards: 1) reconciliation health, 2) late-arrival distribution, 3) top-10 tenants by adjustment volume
Alerts: P1 if apply_failure_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m; P2 if manual_review_queue > 500 items
perf_targets: Memory per worker: < 6GB for 10k concurrent windows
Reconciliation accuracy in shadow run: > 99.8% match to ledger origin after heuristics tuned
